answer: A harbor forge hiring agents to inspect hollow castings can demand a distinct encoded storage replica per voting key. Validators issue unpredictable block challenges and check Merkle proofs against each registered root before a tight deadline; failure suspends that key's votes. Encoding binds the replica to its key, so copying one file cannot serve many identities. Each extra key needs more disk space, even with parallel audits. Security assumes sound replication proofs and a deadline too short to regenerate missing replicas.
